slide.title: Write Once, Reuse Forever
slide.body: One recipe-style card with five short labelled lines (Role, Task, Inputs, Format, Rules) and a teal bookmark tab. Small tag: AI for Freelancers · Lesson 6.

scenes.voiceover: If you type a new prompt every time you need a report, you get a different result every time. The freelancers who save the most time do not write better prompts each day. They write good prompts once, and reuse them.

slide.title: Delivering Work Faster with Prompt Templates
slide.body: AI for Freelancers and Solopreneurs · Lesson 6 of 12

scenes.voiceover: Last time, you built an onboarding pack. Today, we move to the delivery stage, and make your routine client work faster and more consistent.

slide.title: Five parts of a template
slide.body: 1 Role and context · 2 Task · 3 Inputs: [CLIENT TYPE] [DATA] [KEY POINTS] · 4 Format: length, headings, tone · 5 Rules: do not invent figures; mark anything uncertain with [CHECK]

scenes.voiceover: A prompt template is a saved prompt with fixed instructions and blanks that you fill in for each client. A good template has five parts. A role and context. The task. The inputs, which are the blanks you fill in. The format, such as length, headings and tone. And rules, such as do not invent figures.

slide.title: Test and improve
slide.body: Loop: Write template → Test with example input 1, 2, 3 → Spot weak output → Improve → back to Test

scenes.voiceover: Start with your most common deliverables. First drafts, research notes, design briefs or monthly reports. Test each template three times with different example inputs, and improve it when the output is weak.

How much time will you save? It varies a lot by task, by trade, and by how good your inputs are. So do not rely on any general figure. Measure it on your own work, including the time you spend checking. What stays with you is the part clients pay for. The expert decisions, the judgement about what matters, and the final check.

scenes.stock_query: chef tasting sauce in restaurant kitchen
scenes.voiceover: Think of a recipe card in a busy restaurant kitchen. The chef does not invent the sauce again every evening. The recipe gives the same good base each time. But the chef still tastes it and adjusts it before the plate leaves the kitchen.

slide.title: Your template library
slide.body: One document · Name · Date last changed · Example of good output · Inputs: summaries or anonymised figures only

scenes.voiceover: Keep your templates in one document, each with a name, the date you last changed it, and an example of good output. And never put real client secrets or personal data into the inputs. Use summaries or anonymised figures instead.

scenes.stock_query: man reviewing charts on laptop cafe
scenes.on_screen_text: Mateus · social media consultant · Porto Alegre
scenes.voiceover: Let's look at an example. Mateus is a social media consultant in Porto Alegre, Brazil. Every month, he writes a performance report for each of his six small business clients. Each report used to take him about two hours.

slide.title: Mateus's report template
slide.body: You are an assistant to a social media consultant who works with small local businesses. Write a monthly report for a [BUSINESS TYPE] client. Inputs: [FIGURES], [PREVIOUS FIGURES], [MY NOTES]. Format: 1) 3-sentence summary 2) table this month vs last 3) three observations 4) two recommendations, based only on my notes.

scenes.voiceover: His template tells the AI it is an assistant to a social media consultant. The inputs are this month's figures, last month's figures, and his own notes. The format is a three-sentence summary, a comparison table, three observations, and two recommendations based only on his notes.

slide.title: The rules section
slide.body: Rules: use only the figures I give; do not calculate percentages unless I ask; mark anything uncertain with [CHECK]; no marketing jargon. Side note: client names and account details removed.

scenes.voiceover: The rules are the most important part. Use only the figures I give. Do not calculate percentages unless I ask. Mark anything uncertain with the word check. And no marketing jargon. He removes client names and account details, and pastes only his exported figures and his own notes.

slide.title: Mateus times his own work
slide.body: Simple timeline bar: Draft with template (about 10 min) → Check every figure, rewrite recommendations, add one client idea (about 35 min). Caption: his own measurement.

scenes.voiceover: He records his times. The first draft takes about ten minutes. Then he spends about thirty-five minutes checking every figure against his source, rewriting the recommendations in his own words, and adding one idea for each client. That is his own measurement, on his own work.

Notice this. The AI never decides what to recommend. It organises what Mateus already concluded. His expertise is in the observations and the recommendations. That is the part his clients pay for, and it stays with him.

A common mistake is to stop checking once the first few results are good. Templates reduce variation, but AI can still invent a figure or change a number. Keep the use only my inputs rule in every template, and check every number, every time.

slide.title: Key takeaways
slide.body: 1. Role, task, inputs, format, rules. 2. Consistent first drafts; measure your own time saved. 3. You decide and check; no confidential data in the inputs.

scenes.voiceover: Let's recap. First, a prompt template has five parts. Role and context, task, inputs, format and rules. Second, templates give you a consistent first draft for routine work. How much time they save depends on your task, so measure it yourself. Third, you keep the expert decisions and the final check, and you never put confidential client data into the inputs.

scenes.on_screen_text: Next: Quality Checks and Client Confidentiality
scenes.voiceover: Now it is your turn. In the exercise, choose your three most common deliverables and write a template for each, with all five parts. Test each one three times with example data. Then time one task with and without the template, including checking time. In the next lesson, we cover quality checks and client confidentiality.
